slides.0.title: 🏝️ Sardegna
slides.0.subtitle: A Mediterranean “micro-continent” and treasure trove of ancient grapes
slides.1.title: 🏝️ Sardegna at a Glance
slides.1.content:
The second-largest island in the Mediterranean (after Sicilia), often described as a “micro-continent” whose people have a mind-set quite different from the rest of Italy. From the 14th to the 18th century it was under Aragonese-Spanish rule, and grapes such as Cannonau, Carignano and Bovale Sardo, as well as the traditions of fortified wine and flor, all show that Spanish influence.

🏝️
Topography
An irregular succession of mountains, hills, plateaus and plains; the east is more mountainous, with well-worn granite ranges; the west has lower hills with limestone and pockets of volcanic rock and basalt
🏅
Appellations
1 DOCG (Vermentino di Gallura) + 17 DOCs; about half of production is DOC/G
🍇
Vineyards
About 25,000 ha, over 60% red grapes; Cannonau and Vermentino together account for over 40%
🌞
Climate
Mediterranean, with continental influence inland and in the mountains; the Maestrale (Mistral) sweeps the island, and the south-west is the hottest part
slides.2.title: 🗺️ Sardegna DOCG & DOC Interactive Map
slides.3.title: 🍇 Cannonau — Sardegna’s Flagship Red Grape
slides.3.content:
Cannonau is genetically identical to Spain’s Garnacha (Grenache in France). It is grown throughout the island, with its stronghold in Nuoro. High alcohol, red fruit and Mediterranean scrub (macchia); styles range from soft and fruity to serious, complex and well-structured.

Cannonau di Sardegna DOC

🍷 The regional DOC

🗺️ Area: the whole island — the regional appellation for varietal Cannonau

🍇 Grapes: min. 85% Cannonau (most wines are 100%)

👅 Style: from simple and fruity to complex, full-bodied and age-worthy

⏱️ Riserva: min. 2 years’ ageing, at least 6 months in wood

Classico

🏆 Cannonau di Sardegna Classico

🗺️ Area: the historic growing area of Nuoro and Ogliastra

🍇 Grapes: min. 90% Cannonau, with stricter rules on yields, alcohol and ageing

⏱️ Ageing: min. 2 years, at least 1 year in wood

📍 Three official subzones: Oliena, Jerzu, Capo Ferrato
slides.4.title: ⚪ Vermentino di Gallura DOCG
slides.4.content:
Sardegna’s only DOCG and the most important appellation for Vermentino, covering the historic area of Gallura in the north-east. The climate is Mediterranean on the coast, with continental influence inland at higher elevations; the soils are granitic sands atop a granite subsoil.

🤍 Vermentino di Gallura DOCG

Min. 95% Vermentino (most is 100%). Usually vinified in stainless steel; a few producers use wood. Wines range from rich and fruity to intensely mineral and briny.

🏆 Superiore

Lower yields and higher alcohol. The best Vermentino ages well, developing complex flinty-smoky aromas.

🌊 Vermentino di Sardegna DOC

The island-wide regional DOC — together with the Gallura DOCG, one of Vermentino’s two principal appellations. Vermentino is Sardegna’s most widely planted and most important white grape; it favours warm, sunny conditions near the sea and resists wind and drought.
slides.5.title: 🍷 Carignano del Sulcis — Ungrafted Old Vines on Sand
slides.5.content:
One of Sardegna’s most distinctive reds — old, ungrafted alberello vines on loose sandy coastal soils

The appellation lies in Sulcis in south-west Sardegna, including the islands of San Pietro and Sant'Antioco. Hot and dry, it is ideal for Carignano. Carignano is genetically identical to Spain’s Mazuelo (Cariñena) and France’s Carignan, and was most likely brought over from Spain.

🍷 Carignano del Sulcis Rosso

Min. 85% Carignano (many are 100%); Bovale is the go-to blending partner. A fleshy, velvety palate with smooth tannins and lively acidity.

🏆 Superiore and Riserva

Superiore: vines must be trained exclusively as alberello, with higher alcohol and min. 2 years’ ageing. Riserva: min. 2 years’ ageing.
slides.6.title: 🏺 Other Important Sardegna Grapes
slides.6.content:
🔴 Monica

Identity: an ancient grape of unknown origin, Sardegna’s second most widely planted red

History: traditionally used for sweet and fortified wines, now increasingly made as a dry varietal wine

Appellation: Monica di Sardegna DOC, min. 85% Monica; some producers add up to 15% Bovale and/or Carignano; Superiore also exists

⚪ Malvasia di Sardegna

Identity: genetically identical to Malvasia di Lipari (Calabria’s Greco Bianco)

Where: plantings concentrated around Bosa and Cagliari

Appellation: Malvasia di Bosa DOC

⚪ Torbato & 🔴 Cagnulari

Appellation: Alghero DOC, a small area around the town of Alghero in the north-west

Torbato: a rare white grape, made dry or sparkling

Cagnulari: a rare red grape

Also: Alghero DOC allows international grapes such as Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc

🔴 Bovale Sardo

Identity: = Spain’s Graciano, one of the Spanish-influenced grapes

Note: Bovale Grande (Bovale di Spagna) is a different traditional variety

Use: the go-to blending partner in Carignano del Sulcis and the lead grape in the Mandrolisai DOC blend
slides.7.title: 🍯 Sardegna’s Oxidative and Sweet Traditions
slides.7.content:
🍯 Vernaccia di Oristano DOC

Status: Sardegna’s first DOC, with small production

Style: oxidative and Sherry-like, but not fortified; matured under flor in partially filled barrels

Categories: base wine at least 2 years in barrel / Superiore at least 3 / Riserva at least 4

Grape: 100% Vernaccia di Oristano, unrelated to other vines named “Vernaccia”

🍬 Malvasia di Bosa DOC

Area: around Bosa on the central west coast, a tiny production by a few local growers

Grape: min. 95% Malvasia di Sardegna

Rules: min. 13% ABV, medium-sweet to sweet; Riserva min. 15.5% ABV and min. 2 years’ ageing (at least 1 year in wood), sweet to dry, most on the drier side

🍊 Moscato sweet wines

Grape: Moscato Bianco

Appellations: the island-wide Moscato di Sardegna DOC, and Moscato di Sorso-Sennori DOC around the towns of Sorso and Sennori in the north-west

Tradition: Sardegna’s sweet and fortified (liquoroso) wines also trace back to Spanish influence
slides.8.title: 🍽️ Sardegna Food Pairing Guide
slides.8.content:
Sardinian cooking centres on lamb, pork, Pecorino cheese and seafood: porceddu (roast suckling pig), pane carasau flatbread, malloreddus gnocchetti, spaghetti with bottarga, culurgiones dumplings and fregola — shepherding traditions in the mountains living alongside a coastal fishing culture.

🧀 Pecorino Sardo

Sardegna’s hard sheep’s-milk cheese
🍷 With: young cheese with Vermentino di Gallura / aged cheese with Cannonau Riserva
The white’s saline minerality flatters a young cheese; the red’s structure stands up to an aged one

🥚 Spaghetti alla Bottarga

Bottarga is salted, cured grey mullet roe, grated over pasta
🍷 With: Vermentino di Gallura DOCG
A briny, mineral finish echoes the taste of the sea; Vernaccia di Oristano is another classic match

🐷 Porceddu

Whole suckling pig roasted with myrtle (mirto), the soul of festive tables
🍷 With: Cannonau di Sardegna Riserva / Carignano del Sulcis Superiore
Red fruit and Mediterranean herbs echo the myrtle, and the tannins cut the fat

🍝 Malloreddus alla Campidanese

Handmade gnocchetti with a sausage and tomato sauce
🍷 With: Cannonau di Sardegna / Monica di Sardegna
Soft fruit for a homely meat sauce
slides.9.title: 🏺 The History of Sardegna Wine
slides.9.content:
From the nuraghe towers to Spanish and Savoy rule — an island’s own path in wine

Antiquity
The Nuragic civilization: already present before 1800 BC, it left the conical stone towers called nuraghi; vines and wine have been on the island since 1500 BC. The Phoenicians developed viticulture, while the Carthaginians and Romans focused on cereals
14th-18th c.
Aragonese-Spanish rule: the Kingdom of Sardegna was ruled by the Aragonese-Spanish crown, with a lasting influence on grape varieties, fortified wine and flor. The Carta de Logu, the legal code issued by Eleonora, giudice (ruler) of Arborea, also included rules to protect viticulture
18th-19th c.
Savoy and Italian unification: in the 18th century the island passed to the House of Savoy (Piemonte); in 1861 the Kingdom of Sardegna became the Kingdom of Italy. A major vineyard expansion in the 1880s was halted by phylloxera
20th c. to today
From bulk to quality: in the 1940s-50s cooperatives focused on high-alcohol bulk wine; in the 1980s a declining bulk market and the EU vine-pull scheme shrank the vineyard area; in the 1990s the island shifted to quality wine

slides.10.title: 🍇 Cannonau in Depth
slides.10.content:
🧬 Identity and synonyms

Genetically identical to Garnacha (Grenache in France)

Sardegna’s flagship red grape, grown throughout the island, with its stronghold in Nuoro

Other synonyms: Alicante, Gamay del Trasimeno, Tocai Rosso

Together with Vermentino it covers over 40% of the island’s vineyards

📊 Characteristics

Alcohol: high

Aromas: red fruit, Mediterranean scrub

Style: from soft and fruity to serious, complex and well-structured

Training: traditionally alberello (bush vine); modern vineyards also use cordone speronato

The Cannonau spectrum: from soft and fruity to complex and aged

🍒 Soft and fruity

Red berries, strawberry, spice, Mediterranean herbs

Best with: malloreddus with sausage

🍷 Riserva

Min. 2 years’ ageing (at least 6 months in wood); dried herbs, leather, liquorice

Best with: porceddu

🏆 Classico

The historic area of Nuoro and Ogliastra, min. 2 years’ ageing (at least 1 year in wood) — the most structured style

Best with: aged Pecorino Sardo
slides.11.title: ⚪ Vermentino and the Terroir of Gallura
slides.11.content:
Vermentino, of uncertain origin, is Sardegna’s most widely planted and most important white grape. It is aromatic, with fruit, herbs and scrub; full-bodied and high in alcohol, with refreshing acidity and a mineral-saline finish.

🪨

The granite of Gallura

Soils: granitic sands atop a granite subsoil

Landscape: the north-east, with the well-worn granite ranges of the east (such as Monti di Limbara)

Training: Gallura is also one of the typical alberello areas

In the wine: minerality and a briny style

🌊

Climate

Coast: Mediterranean

Inland: continental influence at higher elevations

Wind: the Maestrale (Mistral)

The grape likes: warm, sunny sites near the sea; it resists wind and drought

🏆 Vermentino di Gallura DOCG essentials

Grapes
Min. 95% Vermentino
Most is 100%
Superiore
Lower yields
Higher alcohol
Winemaking
Usually stainless steel
A few use wood
Status
Sardegna’s only DOCG
Top Vermentino appellation
slides.12.title: 🍷 Carignano and the Old Vines of Sulcis
slides.12.content:
🍇 The Carignano grape

Genetically identical to Spain’s Mazuelo (Cariñena) and France’s Carignan

Most likely brought over from Spain; also called Uva di Spagna

Needs warm, sunny, dry conditions to ripen fully, and resists drought and wind

Deep colour, high acidity and tannins

🏖️ The sands of Sulcis

The south-west is the hottest part of the island, with very sandy soils

Phylloxera halted the island’s vineyard expansion in the 1880s, but it struggles to survive in loose sand

So very old ungrafted alberello vines survive on the coastal sands

🌿 Own-rooted alberello vines
Alberello is Sardegna’s traditional training system, typically found in Gallura, Mandrolisai and Sulcis
🍷 Carignano del Sulcis style
A fleshy, velvety palate with smooth tannins and lively acidity
🏝️ The appellation
South-west Sardegna, including the islands of San Pietro and Sant'Antioco
🏆 Superiore
Alberello-trained vines only, higher alcohol, min. 2 years’ ageing
slides.13.title: 🍯 Vernaccia di Oristano in Depth
slides.13.content:
Sardegna’s first DOC — oxidative and Sherry-like, but not fortified

Vernaccia di Oristano is an ancient Sardinian white grape grown in the lower Tirso river valley near Oristano. It prefers warm conditions and alluvial soils, and is unrelated to other vines named “Vernaccia”.

🇮🇹 Vernaccia di Oristano

Soils: alluvial: Bennaxi (deep, fertile) and Gregori (poor, gravelly, free-draining)

Grape: 100% Vernaccia di Oristano

Maturation: after fermentation, moved into oak or chestnut barrels filled to about 80%, where a layer of flor forms

Fortification: none

🇪🇸 Compared with Sherry (Jerez)

Region: Jerez, in Andalucía, Spain

Grape: mainly Palomino

Maturation: the solera system; flor styles such as Fino also mature under a yeast layer

Fortification: fortified

The key to flor: well-ventilated cellars with seasonal temperature swings, where flor produces aldehydes (the Sherry aroma)

🥂 Vernaccia di Oristano

At least 2 years in barrel

Style: intense, complex, oxidative

🏅 Superiore

At least 3 years in barrel

Best with: bottarga, toasted almonds

🏆 Riserva

At least 4 years in barrel; some wines mature for 10 years in a solera-like system

Hallmark: very long-lived
slides.14.title: 🏛️ Leading Sardegna Producers
slides.14.content:
From century-old estates to cooperatives, these producers have taken Sardegna’s native grapes to the world

SM
Historic estate
Sella & Mosca — Est. 1899

The leading estate of the Alghero area, known for the rare white Torbato, and also making Vermentino and Cannonau

🍷 Signature: Alghero DOC Torbato (dry and sparkling)
Alghero DOC’s two rare grapes: Torbato (white) and Cagnulari (red)
AR
Native-grape champion
Argiolas — Est. 1938

Based in Serdiana near Cagliari, expressing the island through native grapes such as Cannonau, Vermentino and Monica

🍷 Flagship: Turriga (a Cannonau-led blend of native grapes)
A symbol of Sardegna’s 1990s shift from bulk wine to quality
Cantina Santadi

An important Sulcis cooperative and a benchmark producer of Carignano del Sulcis

Terre Brune (Carignano-based)
Old vines on sand
Dark fruit, fleshy and smooth
Giovanni Cherchi & Colombu

Producers named in the IWS term list

Giovanni Cherchi: Vermentino and Cagnulari in the north-west
Colombu: Malvasia di Bosa from Bosa
Small-production local styles
💚 Entry level

Regional DOCs

Vermentino di Sardegna, Monica di Sardegna, Cannonau di Sardegna — easy everyday drinking

🧡 Step up

DOCG & old vines

Vermentino di Gallura DOCG, Carignano del Sulcis Superiore, Cannonau Riserva and Classico

❤️ Collector’s

Unique traditions

Vernaccia di Oristano Riserva, Malvasia di Bosa — tiny production, strong personality

slides.16.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.16.points.0: ✓ Sardegna is the second-largest island in the Mediterranean, often called a “micro-continent”; Aragonese-Spanish rule (14th-18th c.) shaped its grapes and its fortified-wine and flor traditions
slides.16.points.1: ✓ About 25,000 ha of vineyards, half of production is DOC/G; over 60% red grapes; 1 DOCG + 17 DOCs
slides.16.points.2: ✓ Mediterranean climate, the Maestrale wind, hottest in the south-west; granitic sands in Gallura (north-east), sandy soils in Sulcis (south-west), alluvial soils around Oristano (west coast)
slides.16.points.3: ✓ The traditional training system is alberello (Gallura, Mandrolisai, Sulcis), with very old ungrafted vines on loose sandy soils
slides.16.points.4: ✓ Cannonau (= Garnacha) is the flagship red: Cannonau di Sardegna DOC min. 85%, Riserva min. 2 years (6 months in wood); Classico min. 90%, 2 years (1 year in wood), subzones Oliena, Jerzu, Capo Ferrato
slides.16.points.5: ✓ Vermentino di Gallura is the only DOCG: min. 95% Vermentino, granitic sands, usually stainless steel; Superiore has lower yields and higher alcohol
slides.16.points.6: ✓ Carignano del Sulcis DOC: min. 85% Carignano (= Mazuelo), with Bovale as blending partner; Superiore is alberello-only with min. 2 years’ ageing
slides.16.points.7: ✓ Vernaccia di Oristano DOC is the first DOC, Sherry-like but not fortified, at least 2/3/4 years in barrel; Malvasia di Bosa and Alghero (Torbato, Cagnulari) add further character

slides.17.questions.1.question: What is special about Vermentino di Gallura?

slides.17.questions.2.options.1: It has very old ungrafted, own-rooted vines

slides.17.questions.3.question: What is bottarga?
slides.17.questions.3.explanation: Bottarga is salted, cured grey mullet roe, a Sardinian delicacy often grated over pasta (spaghetti alla bottarga) and a fine match for Vermentino.
slides.17.questions.4.question: Vermentino di Gallura DOCG is the only DOCG of which region?
slides.17.questions.4.explanation: Vermentino di Gallura DOCG, in Gallura in the north-east, is the only DOCG on the whole island of Sardegna.
slides.17.questions.5.question: What is the traditional vine training system in Sardegna?
slides.17.questions.5.explanation: Alberello (bush vine) is Sardegna’s traditional training system, typically found in Gallura, Mandrolisai and Sulcis.
slides.17.questions.6.question: What is the minimum ageing for Cannonau di Sardegna Riserva?
slides.17.questions.6.options.1: B. 2 years, at least 6 months in wood
slides.17.questions.6.options.2: C. 2 years, at least 1 year in wood
slides.17.questions.6.options.3: D. 3 years, at least 2 years in wood
slides.17.questions.6.explanation: Riserva requires at least 2 years’ ageing, with at least 6 months in wood; 2 years with at least 1 year in wood is the rule for Classico.
slides.17.questions.7.question: Which appellation focuses on the white grape Torbato?
slides.17.questions.7.explanation: Alghero DOC is a small appellation around the town of Alghero featuring varietal wines from two rare grapes: Torbato (white, dry or sparkling) and Cagnulari (red).
slides.17.questions.8.question: Which statement about Vernaccia di Oristano DOC is false?
slides.17.questions.8.options.0: A. It is Sardegna’s first DOC
slides.17.questions.8.options.1: B. It matures under flor in barrels filled to about 80%
slides.17.questions.8.options.2: C. It is a fortified wine
slides.17.questions.8.options.3: D. Riserva spends at least 4 years in barrel
slides.17.questions.8.explanation: Vernaccia di Oristano is oxidative and Sherry-like, but it is not fortified.
slides.17.questions.9.question: Which is NOT an official subzone of Cannonau di Sardegna Classico?
slides.17.questions.9.explanation: Classico has three official subzones: Oliena, Jerzu and Capo Ferrato. Sulcis is the Carignano area in the south-west.
